item.title: Four new arrests in Louvre heist: Two men, two women aged 31–40; $102 mn jewels still missing
item.description: Paris prosecutors announced four more arrests in connection with the $102 million Louvre jewelry heist in October. The four individuals, aged 31-40, are from the Paris region. Investigators believe one of the newly arrested men, already known to police, was a key member of the group that carried out the swift daytime robbery.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: WH dismisses reports of Kash Patel’s firing; Trump poses with FBI director to shut down rumour
item.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt refuted a report claiming President Trump was considering firing FBI Director Kash Patel. Leavitt shared a photo of Trump and Patel together, stating the story was fabricated and Trump laughed at the headline. She asserted that Trump and his team are satisfied with Patel's performance.

Who is Sam Pepper? Firework incident in India leads to streamer’s permanent Kick ban and huge backlash
item.description: London streamer Sam Pepper faced a permanent ban after a firework injured a young girl during his Diwali livestream in New Delhi. The incident occurred on October 20. A rocket went astray, striking the girl near her eye. Pepper apologized and covered medical costs. The platform cited safety concerns for the ban. This event sparks discussions on livestream safety regulations.

item.title: New Zealand officials had to destroy Kash Patel's controversial gifts; toy-inspired guns also illegal
item.description: New Zealand officials faced a dilemma after receiving revolvers from FBI chief Kash Patel, as possessing them is illegal. These "Maverick PG22" firearms, inspired by toy guns, were deemed operable despite their toy-like appearance. The five officials voluntarily surrendered the weapons, which are treated as conventional firearms under New Zealand law, prompting their destruction.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Memoir Misused’: JD Vance’s bestselling book used to smuggle drugs into an Ohio prison
item.description: Vice President JD Vance's memoir, 'Hillbilly Elegy,' was ironically used to smuggle drugs into an Ohio prison. Narcotics were sprayed onto the book's pages and mailed to an inmate, disguised as an Amazon delivery. The scheme was uncovered by investigators, leading to the smuggler's lengthy prison sentence, highlighting innovative drug trafficking methods.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sufficient funds obtained lawfully: Who can apply for Trump Gold Card visa? Form I-140G revealed
item.description: Trump Gold Card visa: To get a Trump Gold Card, an individual must gift $1million to the US and if the application is for a corporate, they must gift the US government $2 million. The petition must establish that the applicants have sufficient funds to make the unrestricted gift to the Department of Commerce; and any funds to be used for the gift have been obtained through lawful means.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Macron spent $1.5m’: Candace Owens alleges French President wants to assassinate her
item.description: Conservative commentator Candace Owens has leveled extraordinary accusations, claiming French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife allegedly allocated $1.5 million for her assassination. Owens further linked alleged Israeli influence to the death of activist Charlie Kirk, suggesting Macron desires her death and that of another journalist. She asserts federal authorities have been notified of these grave threats.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Erika Kirk pregnant? Usha Vance's missing ring? Tracking the crazy rumours swirling in MAGA town
item.description: The internet spent the past week convinced it had uncovered a political soap opera, even though the only thing on display was grief, coincidence and a great deal of imagination. A widow spoke about the future she lost, a vice president offered a public hug and a mother stepped out without her wedding ring. These separate, ordinary moments were stitched together by the MAGAverse into a rumour that Erika Kirk was secretly pregnant and Usha Vance was quietly separating. None of it was true. All of it was loud. The real story was quieter and far more human.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why Trump–Mamdani ‘bromance’ is a ‘nightmare’ for Elise Stefanik’s governor bid
item.description: President Trump's surprisingly cordial meeting with New York City mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani has significantly disrupted Congresswoman Elise Stefanik's gubernatorial campaign. Trump's praise for Mamdani directly contradicts Stefanik's core message, leaving her in a difficult position as she relies on Trump's support while needing to appeal to moderate voters in a Democratic-leaning state.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE sets clear rules for safe and respectful vehicle celebrations on Union Day
item.description: As the UAE prepares for its 54th Union Day, the Ministry of Interior has issued guidelines for safe vehicle celebrations. Only Union Day stickers and the UAE flag are allowed on vehicles, while unsafe or disruptive behaviors like stunts, loud music, or unauthorized modifications are prohibited. Authorities stress respectful flag display, public safety, and cooperation with traffic officers to ensure joyful, hazard-free festivities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Unprecedented and cruel': Trump's announcement of freezing 235,000 Green Cards draws flak
item.description: The announcement from the Trump administration to reassess and possibly cancel Green Cards for 235,000 refugees from the 2021-2025 period has ignited fierce backlash. Critics, including various humanitarian organizations, label this initiative as 'unthinkable and inhumane,' especially at a time when people traditionally express gratitude and compassion during the Thanksgiving week.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: “What are you doing?”: FaZe Lacy’s alarming confrontation with alleged stalker in viral livestream reveals dark side of parasocial fandom
item.description: Twitch streamer FaZe Lacy encountered a woman allegedly stalking him on his livestream, who had previously harassed fellow streamer Stable Ronaldo. The woman, carrying luggage, appeared uninvited in Lacy's neighborhood, making bizarre claims and criticizing his home security. This incident highlights growing security concerns for IRL streamers.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'Came to US with dreams': Friends of Preet Harsoda seek help for treatment, 30 Indian students affected in FSU fire
item.description: A devastating fire at The Social Seminole in Florida has left many Florida State University students, including around 30 Indian students, severely impacted. One student, Preet Harsoda, suffered life-threatening burns and is in intensive care. Many students lost all their belongings, prompting widespread support and fundraising efforts from the university community.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Get out: Greta Thunberg banned from Venice for pouring green dye into Grand Canal in protest
item.description: Greta Thunberg and a group of environmental activists undertook a shocking protest in Venice, dyeing the Grand Canal bright green to raise awareness about insufficient fossil fuel regulations at a UN climate summit. However, their bold actions resulted in a two-day prohibition and fines, as many deemed their approach disrespectful to the historic UNESCO site.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
